## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

- FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

1. **KDA piece-chain floor.** `choose_pieces` takes `min_tokens`; KDA forward and backward pass `chain_min_tokens(reverse)`, 1024 and 192 total tokens, below which the plan runs uncut instead of chaining. The batch-invariant length rule ignores the floor. GDN, GDN2, GDP and the summary engines keep the old rule.
2. **sm90 KDA segment count.** `kda_prefill_sm90._pick_nseg` capped segments at a hardcoded 132 SMs; it now reads the device SM count, and `nseg` joins the compile-cache key (it is baked into the kernel).
3. **Engine-order tripwire.** `test_default_engine_is_frost`: unpinned GDN/KDA graphs run FROST on SM100/103/107, where the cuTile engines also accept them.

## Why

**The KDA chain gate is a one-wave geometry rule with no measurement behind it** (#969 added it). The chain carries passes (summary, state chain, piece-table prologue) whose cost does not shrink with the pieces, and a short sequence does not repay them. KDA's alternative is the uncut schedule; neither depends on the gate values (gates = 1 and random gates time the same within 1-3%).

Chain (old) vs uncut (new), CUDA-graph replay, median of 8 ABBA samples x 50 replays, bf16, d=128, q/k L2 norm in kernel. Selected rows below the floor:

| | shape (B x T, H x HV) | B200 chain us | B200 uncut us | B200 | 68-SM SM100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| KDA fwd | 4x256, 8x8 | 96.4 | 34.9 | 2.76x | (no chain) |
| KDA fwd | 1x256, 32x32 | 94.0 | 35.6 | 2.64x | not run |
| KDA fwd | 1x512, 32x32 | 107.9 | 58.6 | 1.84x | (no chain) |
| KDA fwd | 1x512, 16x16 | 94.2 | 58.8 | 1.60x | 1.89x |
| KDA fwd | 1x768, 16x32 | 119.5 | 80.6 | 1.48x | not run |
| KDA fwd | 1x768, 4x4 | 86.6 | 79.9 | 1.08x | 1.10x |
| KDA bwd | 1x128, 64x64 | 200.6 | 96.4 | 2.08x | not run |
| KDA bwd | 1x128, 32x32 | 152.8 | 94.4 | 1.62x | 2.18x |
| KDA bwd | 1x176, 8x8 | 153.3 | 121.6 | 1.26x | 1.35x |
| KDA bwd | 1x128, 4x4 | 122.3 | 94.8 | 1.29x | 1.33x |

Every measured cell below the floor favours uncut, on both GPUs, with L2 norm on and off (heads 4x4 to 64x64; fwd up to 1x1023, bwd up to 1x191). The closest are 1x1023 fwd and 1x191 bwd at 4 heads on the 68-SM part (0.99x each). Above the floors the comparison turns on head count (fwd 1x1024: 0.94x at 4 heads, 1.27x at 32; bwd 1x256 with L2 norm: 0.83x at 4 heads, 1.54x at 64), so the chain stays there. The floor is on total tokens, so a batch holding one long sequence keeps the chain.

An earlier revision of this PR fit the floors at 2048 / 512 from summed kernel durations (torch.profiler). That overcounts the chain, whose kernels overlap under PDL; under graph replay those floors lost up to 0.60x (fwd 1x2047, 8 heads).

**GDN is left on the old rule.** The earlier revision also dropped the GDN chain in favour of split-K. That measurement used gates of about 0.98 per token, which decay fast enough for split-K to cut anywhere. GDN split-K cuts only where the gates have decayed below e^-10 (`common/split_k.py`), so its cost depends on the data. With gates = 1, or per-head decay rates spread over 1e-4..1e-1 per token, the slow heads cannot be cut and the old revision lost 2-7.7x on long sequences (1x65536, 8x8 bwd: 1.8 ms -> 13.3 ms). Review on this PR found the same on 68- and 148-SM SM100 parts. The chain does not depend on the data; GDN keeps it.

**Engine order.** GDN and KDA had no measured ordering on SM100: whichever engine the family factory lists first wins (manifest slot order does not matter; reordering the slot dict changed nothing, reordering the factory list turned the new test red). Measured on B200 over 136 shapes (fwd and bwd; heads 4x8 to 64x64; T 64 to 64k incl. varlen), FROST led cuTile in GPU time by 1.5-17x everywhere except two small KDA cells at noise level (0.95x, 0.98x), and in eager wall time everywhere (cuTile's per-call host cost is ~250-350 us). The current order is therefore right, so no hook is added; the test keeps it from changing silently.

**Hardcoded SM count.** On a 132-SM H100 `nseg` is unchanged. On 114 SMs (H100 PCIe) 32 heads at N=1 previously launched 4 x 32 = 128 build CTAs, two waves; it now picks 3.

## Related issues

Related to #969 (introduced the piece chain).

Not addressed here: a ragged KDA batch whose `B * HO` reaches the SM count gets a zero slot budget, so its longest sequence runs serially (5 sequences / 28,350 tokens at 32 heads: bwd 11.5 ms vs 7.0 ms for a single 32,768-token sequence). Forcing a larger budget brings it to 5.9 ms; the piece table already cuts by length on device, only the host budget blocks it.

## API and compatibility impact

No API change. Default schedule changes for FROST KDA fwd/bwd without `batch_invariant` below the floors, including `overwrite_initial_state` and `state_indices` calls; results move at bf16 rounding level, not bitwise. `batch_invariant` keeps its schedule and bitwise contract; GDN is unchanged.

Not measured: SM103 and SM107 (the KDA floors were fit on B200 and a 68-SM SM100), 114/78-SM Hopper for the `nseg` change, GDN2 chain gating.

## Testing

Environment: cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CUDA 13.2, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, cuda-tile 1.4.0 with tileiras 13.2.86.

- B200, head `2ecba54cd`: `pytest linear_attention/test_la.py -m "L0 or L1 or L2 or L3 or L4" -k "(frost and (gdn or kda) and not gdn2) or chain_min_tokens or default_engine" -n 6`: 834 passed, 82 skipped. Tests that exercise the chain itself (`test_piece_chain_*`, `schedule="chain"` params) open the floor through an autouse fixture.
- Same suite at the 2048 / 512 floors: 834 passed, 82 skipped.
- B200, earlier head: `-m L0 -k "frost and gdp" -n 6`: 453 passed, 42 skipped (GDP unchanged since).
- H100: `-m "L0 or L1 or L2" -k "hopper and not hopper_cuda and kda"`: 39 passed, 205 skipped (matrix trimming).
- `test_default_engine_is_frost`: RED with the GDN/KDA factory order swapped (2 failed), GREEN restored.

The crossover depends on **runtime decay values**, as well as geometry/device. On a native 148-SM SM100 engineering GPU, BF16 B1/T4096/Hq=Hk=Hv=8/K=V=128 with a nonzero FP32 initial state:

| Gate inputs | Fused Q/K normalization | Previous chain, µs | Current split-K/warmup, µs |
|---|---|---:|---:|

| alpha = 1 | on | 137.26 | 223.29 |
| alpha uniform in (0.5, 1) | on | 136.54 | 97.96 |

This is component replay latency, not serving E2E or qualified B200 performance; environment was FE 1.31, cuDNN 9.27 and DSL 4.8.

The old rule selects 16 chain pieces; the new `(0, 0)` forward window removes the chain regardless of whether decay permits useful cuts. Please retain or narrow the prior GDN chain admission until these inputs are qualified; the KDA and Hopper changes can proceed independently.

- **28 SM100 checks passed**, covering default/window boundaries, batch invariance, aliasing, padded state pools, old/new forward and backward comparisons, changed-Q/V and poisoned-output replay, and the four decay controls. Forward/state used independent FP64 references; backward compared all gradients between prior/current schedules at existing tolerances.
- Short KDA T256/H32 improved 98.43 → 45.23 µs in the same bounded experiment; T1024/H8 was 108.45 → 114.01 µs. Warm Python-op host submission improved in all three initial GDN/KDA comparisons, so the large GDN issue is GPU work.
- **Two native H100 tests passed**, including FP64 O/state, changed-input replay, nonaligned `[1537, 511]` lengths and 4→3→4→3 segment-cache reuse. Hardware actually has 132 SMs; 114 was an injected scheduling budget. This does not establish native 114-SM performance.
- Short KDA overwrite/pool calls do receive the new window, as CodeRabbit noted. Independent in-place and padded-pool tests passed without forcing the chain window open. Please qualify the description's unchanged-schedule statement as applying to GDN; these checks do not call for restoring the old KDA route.

No numerical defect was found in this scope. No independent SM103/SM107 or physical 114/78-SM Hopper validation. I did not start broad CI because the GDN performance boundary needs an owner decision first.

## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.

- [x] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

- FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

## Summary

1. **KDA piece-chain floor.** `choose_pieces` takes `min_tokens`; KDA forward and backward pass `chain_min_tokens(reverse)`, 1024 and 192 total tokens, below which the plan runs uncut instead of chaining. The batch-invariant length rule ignores the floor. GDN, GDN2, GDP and the summary engines keep the old rule.
2. **sm90 KDA segment count.** `kda_prefill_sm90._pick_nseg` capped segments at a hardcoded 132 SMs; it now reads the device SM count, and `nseg` joins the compile-cache key (it is baked into the kernel).
3. **Engine-order tripwire.** `test_default_engine_is_frost`: unpinned GDN/KDA graphs run FROST on SM100/103/107, where the cuTile engines also accept them.

## Why

**The KDA chain gate is a one-wave geometry rule with no measurement behind it** (#969 added it). The chain carries passes (summary, state chain, piece-table prologue) whose cost does not shrink with the pieces, and a short sequence does not repay them. KDA's alternative is the uncut schedule; neither depends on the gate values (gates = 1 and random gates time the same within 1-3%).

Chain (old) vs uncut (new), CUDA-graph replay, median of 8 ABBA samples x 50 replays, bf16, d=128, q/k L2 norm in kernel. Selected rows below the floor:

| | shape (B x T, H x HV) | B200 chain us | B200 uncut us | B200 | 68-SM SM100 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| KDA fwd | 4x256, 8x8 | 96.4 | 34.9 | 2.76x | (no chain) |
| KDA fwd | 1x256, 32x32 | 94.0 | 35.6 | 2.64x | not run |
| KDA fwd | 1x512, 32x32 | 107.9 | 58.6 | 1.84x | (no chain) |
| KDA fwd | 1x512, 16x16 | 94.2 | 58.8 | 1.60x | 1.89x |
| KDA fwd | 1x768, 16x32 | 119.5 | 80.6 | 1.48x | not run |
| KDA fwd | 1x768, 4x4 | 86.6 | 79.9 | 1.08x | 1.10x |
| KDA bwd | 1x128, 64x64 | 200.6 | 96.4 | 2.08x | not run |
| KDA bwd | 1x128, 32x32 | 152.8 | 94.4 | 1.62x | 2.18x |
| KDA bwd | 1x176, 8x8 | 153.3 | 121.6 | 1.26x | 1.35x |
| KDA bwd | 1x128, 4x4 | 122.3 | 94.8 | 1.29x | 1.33x |

Every measured cell below the floor favours uncut, on both GPUs, with L2 norm on and off (heads 4x4 to 64x64; fwd up to 1x1023, bwd up to 1x191). The closest are 1x1023 fwd and 1x191 bwd at 4 heads on the 68-SM part (0.99x each). Above the floors the comparison turns on head count (fwd 1x1024: 0.94x at 4 heads, 1.27x at 32; bwd 1x256 with L2 norm: 0.83x at 4 heads, 1.54x at 64), so the chain stays there. The floor is on total tokens, so a batch holding one long sequence keeps the chain.

An earlier revision of this PR fit the floors at 2048 / 512 from summed kernel durations (torch.profiler). That overcounts the chain, whose kernels overlap under PDL; under graph replay those floors lost up to 0.60x (fwd 1x2047, 8 heads).

**GDN is left on the old rule.** The earlier revision also dropped the GDN chain in favour of split-K. That measurement used gates of about 0.98 per token, which decay fast enough for split-K to cut anywhere. GDN split-K cuts only where the gates have decayed below e^-10 (`common/split_k.py`), so its cost depends on the data. With gates = 1, or per-head decay rates spread over 1e-4..1e-1 per token, the slow heads cannot be cut and the old revision lost 2-7.7x on long sequences (1x65536, 8x8 bwd: 1.8 ms -> 13.3 ms). Review on this PR found the same on 68- and 148-SM SM100 parts. The chain does not depend on the data; GDN keeps it.

**Engine order.** GDN and KDA had no measured ordering on SM100: whichever engine the family factory lists first wins (manifest slot order does not matter; reordering the slot dict changed nothing, reordering the factory list turned the new test red). Measured on B200 over 136 shapes (fwd and bwd; heads 4x8 to 64x64; T 64 to 64k incl. varlen), FROST led cuTile in GPU time by 1.5-17x everywhere except two small KDA cells at noise level (0.95x, 0.98x), and in eager wall time everywhere (cuTile's per-call host cost is ~250-350 us). The current order is therefore right, so no hook is added; the test keeps it from changing silently.

**Hardcoded SM count.** On a 132-SM H100 `nseg` is unchanged. On 114 SMs (H100 PCIe) 32 heads at N=1 previously launched 4 x 32 = 128 build CTAs, two waves; it now picks 3.

## Related issues

Related to #969 (introduced the piece chain).

Not addressed here: a ragged KDA batch whose `B * HO` reaches the SM count gets a zero slot budget, so its longest sequence runs serially (5 sequences / 28,350 tokens at 32 heads: bwd 11.5 ms vs 7.0 ms for a single 32,768-token sequence). Forcing a larger budget brings it to 5.9 ms; the piece table already cuts by length on device, only the host budget blocks it.

## API and compatibility impact

No API change. Default schedule changes for FROST KDA fwd/bwd without `batch_invariant` below the floors, including `overwrite_initial_state` and `state_indices` calls; results move at bf16 rounding level, not bitwise. `batch_invariant` keeps its schedule and bitwise contract; GDN is unchanged.

Not measured: SM103 and SM107 (the KDA floors were fit on B200 and a 68-SM SM100), 114/78-SM Hopper for the `nseg` change, GDN2 chain gating.

## Testing

Environment: cuDNN 9.27.0.42, CUDA 13.2, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.8.0, cuda-tile 1.4.0 with tileiras 13.2.86.

- B200, head `2ecba54cd`: `pytest linear_attention/test_la.py -m "L0 or L1 or L2 or L3 or L4" -k "(frost and (gdn or kda) and not gdn2) or chain_min_tokens or default_engine" -n 6`: 834 passed, 82 skipped. Tests that exercise the chain itself (`test_piece_chain_*`, `schedule="chain"` params) open the floor through an autouse fixture.
- Same suite at the 2048 / 512 floors: 834 passed, 82 skipped.
- B200, earlier head: `-m L0 -k "frost and gdp" -n 6`: 453 passed, 42 skipped (GDP unchanged since).
- H100: `-m "L0 or L1 or L2" -k "hopper and not hopper_cuda and kda"`: 39 passed, 205 skipped (matrix trimming).
- `test_default_engine_is_frost`: RED with the GDN/KDA factory order swapped (2 failed), GREEN restored.
